# Page 15^page=15
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 15 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Union Cabinet Approves Extension of Stand-Up India Scheme Until 31 March 2031 with Rs 4,111 Crore In November 2026, the Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved the continuation of the Stand-Up India scheme for an additional period of another 5 years, extending its implementation until 31 March 2031, with a Rs 4,111 crore credit guarantee corpus to promote entrepreneurship among women, Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Union Cabinet approves extension of Stand-Up India Scheme ✓ Extension till: 31 March 2031 ✓ Objective: Promote entrepreneurship among women, SC, ST ✓ Credit Guarantee Corpus: Rs 4,111 crore ✓ Implementation Agency: DFS, MoF ✓ Enterprises: Greenfield projects ✓ Loan Amount: Rs 10 lakhs to Rs 1 Cr ✓ Credit guarantee: 85% of credit, Guarantee fee – 0.50% ✓ Facilitated loans to: 2.75 lakh women, SC, ST ✓ Repayment: 7 years, Moratorium – 18 months. About Stand Up India Scheme: Objective: The scheme, launched on 5 April 2016, aims to provide financial assistance to additional 2.5 lakh entrepreneurs in a span of five years. Implementation Agency: The Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance (MoF), is responsible for implementing the scheme. Bank Coverage: The scheme is implemented through Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs). Enterprises: Loans under the scheme are available for greenfield projects only, i.e. the beneficiary’s first time venture in the following sectors: • Manufacturing, Services, Trading and Agri-allied activities Eligibility: The applicant must be over 18 years old and in case of non-individual enterprises at least 51% of the shareholding and controlling stake should be held by either an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur. Loan Type: The loan can be in the form of either: • Composite – Working Capital and Term Loan (Or) • Term Loan Loan Amount: Under this scheme, the eligible entrepreneurs can avail loans of above Rs 10 lakhs and up to Rs 1 Crore (Cr) for setting up new business. Credit Guarantee: To facilitate the credit flow, the scheme provides credit guarantee coverage of 85% of the loan amount. • A standard guarantee fee of 0.50% is applicable. Progress: The scheme which was launched in April 2016, has so far facilitated loans to more than 2.75 lakh women, SC and ST entrepreneurs. • The Cabinet also approved a Credit Guarantee Corpus of Rs. 4,111 Cr for the scheme. Repayment: The loan is repayable in 7 years with a maximum moratorium period of 18 months.

Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 16 Daily Content PDF About Ministry of Finance (MoF): Union Minister – Nirmala Sitharaman (Rajya Sabha – Karnataka) Minister of State – Pankaj Chaudhary (Constituency – Maharajganj, Uttar Pradesh, UP) GoI Extends PLI Scheme for Medical Devices Until FY36 with Rs 2,700 Crore Outlay In November 2026, the Government of India (GoI) decided to extend the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Promoting Domestic Manufacturing of Medical Devices (PLI-MD) until Financial Year 2035-36 (FY36), with an approved outlay of Rs 2,700 crore. • The Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP) under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (MoC&F) has invited the fresh applications for the revamped PLI-MD 2.0 through an online portal scheduled to be launched within 10 days of the announcement. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Extension of PLI-MD scheme ✓ Extended by: GoI ✓ Extended Tenure: FY36 ✓ Purpose of Scheme: To promote local manufacturing of medical devices ✓ Total Budget Outlay: Rs 2,700 crore ✓ Gestation Period: 3 years ✓ Target Segments (TS): 04 ✓ Incentives: Offers approximately 5% for TS1, 9% for TS2 and TS3, and 6% for TS4, based on technical complexity. ✓ Key Changes: Removed the minimum sales threshold for claiming incentives and relaxed the minimum investment requirement. Key Details of PLI-MD 2.0: Aim: PLI-MD 2.0 aimed to strengthen domestic manufacturing of critical components and reduce India’s dependence on imported medical technology. Gestation Period: As per the revised programme, the eligible applicants will be allowed 3 years for setting up their manufacturing facilities in any of the 4 Target Segments (TS). Target Segments: Target Segments (TS) of the scheme are: TS1 (medical consumables, disposables and implants); TS2 (critical components); TS3 (high-end medical devices which are presently at a nascent stage of local manufacturing); TS4 (high-end medical devices that are presently only assembled in the country). • Incentive Structure: The scheme provides targeted incentive rates across all 4 TS, based on the degree of technical complexity such as: averaging approximately 5% for TS1; nearly 9% for TS2 and TS3; and 6% for TS4. Further, applicants can submit multiple applications across one or more of the 4 TS. Key Relaxations: Under the extended programme, the GoI discontinued the minimum sales threshold requirement to claim incentive and has also reduced the minimum investment requirement. PLI-MD 2.0: The key objectives of the scheme is to develop indigenous supply chains, attract investment, generate employment, improve quality of Made in India devices, reduce price of medical devices, and enhance India’s global competitiveness in high-end medical technologies. About PLI-MD Scheme: Background: Originally, the scheme was launched in FY21 by DoP, MoC&F, for a period of 8 years i.e. from FY21 to 28, aimed to provide financial incentive to boost domestic manufacturing and attract large investments in the medical device sector, Key Progress: So far, the scheme has led to domestic manufacturing of more than 60 high end medical devices and components, including X-ray tubes and detectors, 1.5T MRI, Linear Accelerator (LINAC), Computed Tomography (CT) scanners, mammography machines, among others and has resulted in production valued at over Rs 16,000 crore. About Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (MoC&F): Union Minister- Jagat Prakash (JP) Nadda (Rajya Sabha- Gujarat) Minister of State (MoS)- Anupriya Patel (Constituency- Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, UP) Union Cabinet Approves Continuation of CGFMU Under PMMY Till March 2031 with Rs 5,000 Crore Corpus In November 2026, the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved the continuation of the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) for five years until 31 March 2031, with a Rs 5,000 crore corpus to facilitate Rs 12.6 lakh crore in loans under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY). • The extended scheme will cover all loans sanctioned under PMMY during the XVIth Finance Commission (16th FC) cycle, from Financial Year 2026–27 (FY27) to FY31. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Approval for continuation of CGFMU for 5 years ✓ By Whom? Union Cabinet, chaired by PM Narendra Modi ✓ Extended Until: 31 March 2031 (FY27 to FY31, XVIth Finance Commission cycle) ✓ Corpus: Rs 5,000 crore ✓ Scheme: Under PMMY ✓ Credit Support: Rs 12.6 lakh crore ✓ Implementing Trustee: NCGTC ✓ Revised Guarantee Fee: 0.75% per annum (earlier 1%) About Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU): Launch: CGFMU was launched by the Government of India (GoI) in January 2016 and is sponsored by the Department of Financial Services (DFS) under the Ministry of Finance (MoF). Structure: The fund is managed by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC), a wholly-owned Government of India company, which provides credit guarantee coverage to Lending Institutions (LIs) against default risks on eligible loans under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY). Coverage: The scheme guarantees loans of up to Rs 20 lakh to eligible micro enterprises under PMMY, overdrafts of up to Rs 10,000 provided by banks through Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) accounts, and loans to Self-Help Groups (SHGs) with portfolio sizes ranging from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 20 lakh.

# Page 18^page=18
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 18 Daily Content PDF Guarantee: Coverage is linked to the disbursed amount for working capital limits and the outstanding amount for term loans, reflecting the actual credit-risk exposure of lending institutions. • Fee: The annual guarantee fee has been reduced from 1% to 0.75%, while the fee structure for SHGs remains unchanged at 0.25% in the first year and 0.50% in subsequent years. Performance: As of September 2026, lending institutions had sanctioned over 60.36 crore loans worth Rs 43.34 lakh crore under PMMY, while CGFMU’s credit-guarantee mechanism strengthens collateral-free lending, expands formal banking access for micro entrepreneurs, and supports entrepreneurship, business growth and employment generation. About Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY): Launch: It was launched on 8 April 2015 by the GoI to provide collateral-free institutional credit of up to Rs 20 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises, with the objective of achieving “Fund the Unfunded” by bringing small businesses into the formal banking system. Loan Categories: PMMY loans are classified into four categories based on financing requirements: • Shishu: Loans up to Rs 50,000. • Kishore: Loans above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh. • Tarun: Loans above Rs 5 lakh and up to Rs 10 lakh. • Tarun Plus: Loans above Rs 10 lakh and up to Rs 20 lakh, available to entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid previous loans under the Tarun category. Tarun Plus Introduction: The Tarun Plus category became effective on 24 October 2024, increasing the maximum PMMY loan limit from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 20 lakh for eligible borrowers. Eligibility: Indian citizens aged between 18 and 65 years with a viable business plan and no previous loan defaults are eligible to apply for financial assistance under the scheme National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC): Trusts: NCGTC manages multiple credit guarantee funds and schemes, including: • Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Educational Loans (CGFEL), • Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Skill Development (CGFSD), • Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Factoring (CGFF), • Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU), • Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand Up India (CGFSI). Chief Executive Officer (CEO) – Damodar Mishra Headquarters – Mumbai, Maharashtra Established – March 28, 2014 Union Cabinet Approves NBS Rates for Rabi 2026-27 on P&K Fertilizers with Rs. 62,370.02 Crore Budget On November 11 2026, the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) fertilisers for the Rabi Season (2026–2027) with an estimated budgetary requirement of Rs. 62,370.02 crore, covering the period from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. • The Union Cabinet also approved an 8.449-km (kilometre) Noida Metro Aqua Line extension from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector-04, Uttar Pradesh (UP) and the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at the historic North and South Block Complex in New Delhi, Delhi at an estimated cost of Rs. 3,230 crore. NBS Approval: Background: Implemented on 1 April 2010, governed by the NBS scheme, it covers 28 grades of P&K fertilisers, including Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP), Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium and Sulphur (NPKS) grades, and other eligible grades. Budget: The estimated allocation increased by Rs. 24,417.73 crore, from Rs. 37,952.29 crore in Rabi Season 2025–26. Subsidy Disbursement: The subsidy rates, rationalised in view of international prices, will be disbursed to fertiliser manufacturers and importers throughout the six-month Rabi season, enabling them to supply fertilisers to farmers at reasonable prices. Extension of Noida Metro Aqua Line: Connectivity: The Rs 2,390 crore Aqua Line extension, comprising five elevated stations, will increase the combined active Metro network of Noida and Greater Noida to 71.878 km, improving connectivity to residential, commercial, industrial, educational, healthcare and residential areas, including an interchange at Noida Sector-61 Blue Line. Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum (YYBM) at the North and South Block Complex, New Delhi. Background: The PM Narendra Modi announced the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum (YYBM) on 18 May 2023, and the Public Investment Board (PIB) appraised its proposal on 27 July 2026, with the Ministry of Culture concurring with the recommendations. Infrastructure: The project spans approximately 1,78,509 square metres (sq. m) of built-up area, with over 1 lakh sq. m of exhibition space, expected to be the world’s largest museum display area. Museum Collection: Around 1.8 million objects have been identified for potential display, sourced from the National Museum, Ministry of Culture museums, 52 Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) site museums, state museums and private collections. Implementation: The museum will be developed in phases from Financial Year 2026-2027 (FY27) to (FY31), with its first gallery, themed ‘Adornment’, being established in the North Block and expected to open to public in the latter half of 2027, equipped to handle a visitor flow of 1 crore visitors in a year. About Archaeological Survey of India (ASI): Role: ASI is responsible for conducting archaeological research and protecting and conserving India’s archaeological heritage. Framework: Operates under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958, and administers the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972. Founded: 1861 by Alexander Cunningham

Exam Hints: ✓ What? Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026 (IPRD-2026) ✓ Organiser: Indian Navy & NMF ✓ Where? New Delhi, Delhi ✓ Theme: ‘Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific’ ✓ Focus: Maritime security, ocean governance and emerging technologies ✓ India’s Maritime Vision: MAHASAGAR About Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026 (IPRD-2026): Governance: The session Collaborative Approaches to Ocean Governance and Maritime Resilience covered ocean governance, equitable deep-sea research, resource management, resilient island infrastructure under the Infrastructure for Resilient Island States (IRIS) programme and marine science–shipping cooperation. Technology: The session Transformative Maritime Technologies and Dual-Use Implications discussed Artificial Intelligence (AI), quantum technologies, responsible governance of dual-use technologies, emerging technology adoption by smaller navies and Navy-to-Navy cooperation. Special Sessions and Publication: The conference featured ‘Sahyog Ka Samvaad’, an ambassadorial interaction, and ‘Perspectives from the Flag Bridge’ with former naval chiefs, alongside the release of a monograph titled Sea Blindness and Maritime Heritage in India. Collaboration: Discussions highlighted Filipino expertise in ocean governance, equitable deep-sea research partnerships, resource governance, resilient infrastructure for vulnerable island states and stronger links between marine science and shipping operations. Outcomes: IPRD-2026 identified actionable outcomes under the Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation pillar of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) and reinforced India’s commitment to maritime security, ocean governance and resilience through its MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) vision. About IPOI: Launch: Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi proposed the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) at the 14th East Asia Summit (EAS) held in Bangkok, Thailand, on 4 November 2019. Objective: An open, non-treaty-based initiative aimed at promoting a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific through maritime security, sustainable development and regional cooperation. # Page 21^page=21
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 21 Daily Content PDF Defence Exercise Sea Vigil-26 from 11 to 19 November 2026 to assess and strengthen India’s maritime security and coastal defence preparedness. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Pan-India Coastal Defence Exercise “Sea Vigil-26” ✓ Edition: Fifth edition. ✓ Coordinating Agency: Indian Navy. ✓ Duration: 11–19 November 2026. ✓ Phases: CDSRE and Sea Phase. ✓ Coverage: Entire Indian coastline and EEZ. ✓ Participants: IN, ICG, Coastal Security Police, Customs and other maritime agencies. ✓ Linked Exercise: TROPEX. Key Highlights of Sea Vigil-26: Coordination: The IN is coordinating Sea Vigil-26 as the lead agency, bringing together central and state agencies to evaluate India’s coastal security arrangements. Phases: The exercise is being conducted in two phases: Coastal Defence and Security Readiness Evaluation (CDSRE) Phase from 11 to 17 November, followed by the Sea Phase on 18 and 19 November 2026. Participants: The 2026 edition involves assets of the IN, Indian Coast Guard (ICG), Coastal Security Police, Customs and other maritime agencies, along with fishing and coastal communities. • It is supported by five Union Ministries, Ministry of Defence (MoD), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG), and Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAHD). Coverage: It spans India’s entire coastline and EEZ, involving all coastal States and Union Territories (UTs), fishing communities and other maritime stakeholders. Background: Exercise Sea Vigil was conceptualised in 2018 following the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks to validate coastal security measures, with its inaugural edition held in January 2019, subsequent editions in 2021, 2022 and 2024, and serves as a precursor to the Indian Navy’s biennial Theatre Level Readiness Operational Exercise (TROPEX). About Indian Navy (IN): Overview: The IN is the maritime branch of the Indian Armed Forces, responsible for protecting India’s maritime borders, securing international trade routes, and projecting strategic influence across the Indo- Pacific. Command: The President of India serves as the Supreme Commander, while operational command is led by the four-star Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS). • Its modern blue-water fleet operates two aircraft carriers (INS Vikrant and INS Vikramaditya), nuclear-powered and conventional submarines, and stealth warships. Chief of Naval Staff (CNS) – Admiral Krishna Swaminathan (27th CNS) Headquarters – New Delhi, Delhi Established – 26 January 1950. Nasha Mukt Yuva Par Paricharcha: MY Bharat organised 85 programmes and 298 activities through block-level Neighbourhood Youth Parliaments (NYPs), engaging 9,526 participants in discussions on substance abuse, awareness sessions, street plays, slogan writing and anti-drug pledges. Diwali Sneh Milan: MY Bharat and the National Service Scheme (NSS), under the MYAS, organised nationwide ‘Diwali Sneh Milan’ celebrations across 153 institutions, recording 1,07,494 participations to promote drug-free festivities, substance abuse awareness and community engagement. MoD Signs Rs.498.58 crore Contract with CSL for INS Betwa Upgrade On 11 November 2026, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) signed a contract worth Rs.498.58 crore (approximately Rs.500 crore) with Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) for the Normal Refit and Re-powering of the Indian Naval Ship (INS) Betwa, a Brahmaputra-class frigate of the Indian Navy (IN). • The contract was signed in the presence of Rajesh Kumar, Secretary Singh, MoD in New Delhi, Delhi. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Contract signed for INS Betwa refit and re-powering ✓ Who? MoD and CSL ✓ Contract Value: Rs 498.58 crore ✓ In Presence of: Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh ✓ Key Upgrade: Steam-to-diesel propulsion conversion. About INS Betwa Upgrade: Objective: To enhance INS Betwa’s operational effectiveness through propulsion transformation and combat system upgrades.
